output.reason: Mild one-day scratchy throat with reported no fever and no trouble swallowing, no reported functional impairment, can be managed with over-the-counter symptom relief and a clear worsening safety net.
output.patientMessage: You can manage this at home now: try throat lozenges, plenty of fluids, gargling, and an over-the-counter pain reliever per label. A mild scratchy throat lasting a day is usually a self-limited viral irritation. Message a clinician here if the sore throat lasts more than two days or you feel very unwell, and get emergency care right away for trouble breathing, drooling, or a lot of trouble swallowing.
differential: Streptococcal pharyngitis (less likely without fever, but not excluded)
output.vitalSigns: No vital-sign values reported; whether any were measured is unknown, though he reports "no fever".
output.evidenceLimitations: Consumer health summaries support general self-care and warning signs, not individualized diagnosis or exclusion of strep.
